introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (headed "One hour 30 minutes" on page 2): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (40 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (50 minutes): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
In the process of producing LASERs, atoms of the active medium are excited from the ground state, $n = 1$ (of energy $E_1 = -11.2\ \mathrm{eV}$) to $n = 3$ (of energy $E_3 = -1.38\ \mathrm{eV}$). These atoms then fall back momentarily to $n = 2$ (of energy $E_2 = -5.82\ \mathrm{eV}$). They are then stimulated by a suitable energy photon to fall back to the $n = 1$ level.

Define the following words and expressions used in relation to LASERs

La raie laser est lue comme la transition stimulée n = 2 vers n = 1 (231 nm) ; la transition 3 vers 2 donnerait 280 nm, mais le texte dit que c'est la chute vers n = 1 qui est stimulée.

questions.corrige_markdown: **Optical pumping** is the use of an intense source of light (a flash lamp, or another laser) to supply energy to the atoms of the active medium so that many of them are raised from the ground state to higher (excited) energy levels, from which they drop to a long-lived (metastable) level. It is the process that builds up the excited population needed for laser action.

questions.enonce_markdown: Population inversion as used in the production of LASERs.
questions.corrige_markdown: **Population inversion** is the condition in which more atoms of the active medium are in a higher (metastable) energy level than in the lower level to which they will fall, in particular more atoms in $n = 2$ than in the ground state $n = 1$. In normal thermal equilibrium the lower level is the more populated. With an inversion, stimulated emission exceeds absorption, so the light passing through the medium is amplified instead of being absorbed.

questions.enonce_markdown: Explain why the LASER beam has a high intensity and calculate the wavelength of the light produced.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Why the intensity is high.** Stimulated emission produces photons that are identical to the stimulating photon: same frequency (the light is monochromatic), same direction and in phase with it, so the light is **coherent**. The waves therefore superpose constructively and their amplitudes add, so the intensity grows as the square of the combined amplitude, instead of adding photon by photon as it does for incoherent light. The mirrors of the optical cavity make the light pass many times through the medium, causing an avalanche of stimulated emissions, and only light travelling along the axis is kept, so the beam is narrow and parallel with almost no spread. The power is therefore concentrated in a very small area, which gives a high intensity (power per unit area).

**Wavelength.** The laser light is emitted in the stimulated transition $n = 2 \to n = 1$. (The momentary fall $n = 3 \to n = 2$ is the quick step that fills the metastable level, not the laser line.) Constants used: $h = 6.63\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}$, $c = 3.00\times10^{8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $1\ \mathrm{eV} = 1.60\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}$.

$$\Delta E = E_2 - E_1 = -5.82 - (-11.2) = 5.38\ \mathrm{eV} = 5.38\times1.60\times10^{-19} = 8.61\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{J}$$

$$\lambda = \frac{hc}{\Delta E} = \frac{6.63\times10^{-34}\times3.00\times10^{8}}{8.61\times10^{-19}} = 2.31\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{m}$$

**Wavelength $\approx 231\ \mathrm{nm}$** (ultraviolet).
